chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Zaynab the Perfumer, the round-faced one, came to the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his daughters, and she used to sell perfume to them. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came while she was with them, so he said: 'When you come to us, our houses become fragrant.' She said: 'Your houses are more fragrant due to your scent, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'When you sell, do so well and do not cheat, for it is more pious and preserves the wealth.' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I did not come with anything from my selling, but rather I came to ask you about the Magnificence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' He said: 'Majestic is the Majesty of Allah. I will tell you about some of that.'

Then he said: 'This earth, with what is upon it, compared to that which is beneath it, is like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis. And these two, with what is in them and upon them, compared to that which is beneath them, is like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis. And the third, until it reached the seventh.' And he recited this Verse: 'He created seven heavens and of the earth a similar number to them.'

And the seven earths, with what is in them and upon them, are upon the back of the rooster, like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis. And the rooster has two wings: a wing in the East and a wing in the West, and its legs are at the fringes. And the seven [heavens] and the rooster, with the rooster, with what is in them and upon them, are upon the rock, like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis.

And the rock, with what is in it and upon it, is upon the back of the whale, like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis. And the seven [heavens] and the rooster and the rock and the whale, with what is in them and upon them, are upon the dark ocean, like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis.

And the seven [heavens] and the rooster and the rock and the whale and the dark ocean are upon the outgoing air, like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis. And the seven [heavens] and the rooster and the rock and the whale and the dark ocean and the air are upon the soil (al-thara), like a ring thrown in a desert of Qis.
To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is beneath the soil.

Then the report ended at the soil. And the seven [heavens] and the rooster and the rock and the whale and the dark ocean and the air and the soil, with what is in them and upon them, compared to the first sky, are like a ring in a desert of Qis.

And all of this, and the sky of the world, with what is upon it and in it, compared to that which is above it, is like a ring in a desert of Qis. And these two skies, with what is in them and upon them, compared to that which is above them, is like a ring in a desert of Qis. And these three, with what is in them and upon them, compared to the fourth, is like a ring in a desert of Qis, until it reached the seventh.

And they [the seven heavens] and what is in them and upon them, compared to the ocean hidden from the people of the earth, are like a ring in a desert of Qis. And these seven and the hidden ocean, compared to the mountains of hail, are like a ring in a desert of Qis.
And He sends down from the sky, mountains within which is hail.

And these seven and the hidden ocean and the mountains of hail, compared to the air in which the hearts are confused, are like a ring in a desert of Qis. And these seven and the hidden ocean and the mountains of hail and the air, compared to the veils of light, are like a ring in a desert of Qis.
And these seven and the hidden ocean and the mountains of hail and the air and the veils of light, compared to the Chair (al-Kursi), are like a ring in a desert of Qis.
His Chair (Kursi) encompasses the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.

And these seven and the hidden ocean and the mountains of hail and the air and the veils of light and the Chair, compared to the Throne, are like a ring in a desert of Qis. And he recited this Verse: 'The Beneficent, Who is established on the Throne.'
And in the narration of al-Hasan: 'The veils [are] before the air in which the hearts are confused.'

key_terms.الثَّرَى: The soil/ground, often cited in Quranic verses regarding the earth's depth
key_terms.الدِّيكُ: The Rooster, a creature supporting the earths in this cosmology
key_terms.الْبَحْرُ الْمُظْلِمُ: The dark ocean, a layer in the cosmic hierarchy
key_terms.الْحُوتُ: The Whale, supporting the rock upon which the rooster stands
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne, the highest created entity mentioned in this narration
key_terms.الْكُرْسِيُّ: The Chair (Kursi), a vast entity encompassing the heavens and earth
key_terms.حُجُبُ النُّورِ: Veils of Light, spiritual barriers or layers in the cosmic structure
key_terms.فَلَاةٌ قِيٌّ: A vast, empty desert, used as a simile for insignificance

ai.seo_question: What is the cosmological hierarchy of the universe according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* presents a layered cosmological model where each celestial or elemental stratum is rendered insignificant compared to the one above it, culminating in the Divine Throne (*Al-Arsh*). It serves as a profound theological illustration of Allah's infinite majesty and the relative smallness of creation, reinforcing the concept of *Tawhid* through spatial metaphor.
